title: Work begins on UK’s new £750m supercomputer
summary: Construction work has started on the UK’s new £750m national supercomputer.

title: BOI Director General Renuka Weerakone retires
summary: Director General of the Board of Investment (BOI) of Sri Lanka, Renuka M. Weerakone, retired from her position on June 25, bringing to a close a distinguished 32-year career at the country’s premier investment promotion agency, the BOI said.

title: Two Indian witnesses to be summoned in Namal’s Krrish deal case
summary: The Colombo High Court today ordered summons to be issued to two Indian nationals to provide evidence in the controversial Krrish deal case involving Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa.

title: Speaker reaffirms Parliament’s support for National Commission on Women
summary: Speaker Dr. Jagath Wickramaratne has reaffirmed Parliament’s commitment to providing every possible support to strengthen the work of the National Commission on Women and safeguard its independence.

title: Rohitha Rajapaksa leaves CCIB after five-hour statement
summary: Rohitha Rajapaksa, the son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, left the Central Crime Investigation Bureau (CCIB) after nearly five hours, having recorded a statement in connection with an investigation into an investment he had made in an institution located in Mirihana.

title: In Colombo, Bangkok this week, India and Pakistan met again for track 2 talks
summary: Indian and Pakistani delegates have held a fresh round of Track Two diplomacy talks in Colombo and Bangkok earlier this week. The primary objective was to strengthen mechanisms for dialogue during crises, alongside measures to prevent and manage potential escalations. During the meetings both sides exchanged notes, and had frank exchanges on issues related to terrorism and water.

title: Court of Appeal enters digital era with historic first E-Filing case
summary: Sri Lanka’s judicial system marked a historic milestone today as the Court of Appeal successfully accepted and heard its first-ever electronic filing (E-Filing) case, ushering in a new era of digital justice and paperless court administration.

title: FIFA suspends Nepal over third-party interference
summary: World football’s governing body FIFA has suspended Nepal’s football association, officials said Thursday, barring the country from all international competitions.

title: Media will not survive if they don’t come out of garbage pile: President
summary: The media will not survive in this society if they fail to come out of the garbage pile they have put themselves into, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake told Parliament today.

title: Oil price falls to levels not seen since before Iran war
summary: The price of oil has fallen to levels not seen since before the Iran war as traffic through the key Strait of Hormuz shipping route gradually resumes.

title: UN, WFP officials meet Defence Secretary to discuss disaster resilience
summary: The United Nations Resident Coordinator in Sri Lanka, Marc-André Franche, and the World Food Programme (WFP) Representative and Country Director, Philip Ward, met with Defence Secretary Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha (Retd) at the Ministry of Defence.

title: IOC Launches Historic $140M Athlete Grant Programme
summary: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has announced a landmark $140 million funding programme that will provide a $10,000 grant to every eligible Olympian competing at the Games.

title: Sri Lanka to receive four new cath labs worth Rs. 1.2Bn
summary: Sri Lanka’s state hospital system is set to receive four modern catheterisation laboratory (cath lab) units within the next week, the Ministry of Health and Mass Media said.

title: PTA will be abolished in a few months: President
summary: The Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) will be abolished in a few months, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake told Parliament today.

title: Iran warns ships it’s ‘unacceptable and dangerous’ to transit the Strait of Hormuz without their approval
summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned shipowners on Wednesday that any new transit route through the Strait of Hormuz established without coordination with Tehran is “unacceptable and dangerous,” threatening actions against vessels that ignore its instructions.
